text:
Today I sat in the Apple Store for over 2 hours, trying to get a repair done on my AppleCare covered AirPod Pros 2, only to hear "we can't help, but we can give you a discount on some new ones" -- even though it's their system that screwed up. 

I was also on the phone with Apple Support at the same time for well over an hour, while in store, trying to help sort it out on their behalf.

The fix is simple. Just replace the left earbud. 
But they wouldn't even run the full diagnostic because -- get this -- at the start of the month, I had an initial repair done through their authorized service provider (scheduled thru Apple's website). It was covered under AppleCare. They sent it to Apple to run the diagnostic, who sent it back within a week with a new case.

This didn't solve the issue ultimately, as the left earbud is basically dead and won't connect to my phone.

The trouble is, the new case has a new serial number, and for whatever reason (no one can tell me), the stupid support ticket was never closed; which in AppleLand means my AppleCare (still good through 2027 btw) never actually transferred to the new case. 

So the original repair shop handed me back my airpods, signed off on the free "repair", and then my airpods were no longer covered under AppleCare. In fact they weren't even tied to my Apple account at that point(!!)

The old case (now in Apple's possession), is covered under AppleCare instead.

SO - now I'm back at the mall two weeks later, for a second go around. 

After the first genius told me he couldn't help until I called the first repair shop (which said they did everything right), I got upleveled to senior support over the phone to get them to do a backend fix to transfer the AppleCare coverage... Which can take days to process, meaning I'd have to go back in a third time!

The senior support tech was kind enough to see if she could get a special authorization code so they could do the swap without my AppleCare plan propagated to the current case, but no such luck.

Meanwhile, everyone (including the two separate GENIUSES I had appointments with today) knows i have applecare coverage and should be able to just give me a new left earbud. 

But they wouldn't. And the most offensive part is the manager apparently offered to give me a discount on new Airpods Pro 3 if I wanted instead, as if that would be a solve here.

@johnternus if for some reason you're reading this, please consider giving Apple Support and the reps in store more latitude in cases like this. I can't help but feel like they're handstrung by a system so large it can't handle basic customer support needs. 

As a customer, I shouldn't have to be the arbiter.

I completely understand that weird shit happens in the backend sometimes but a clerical error should not result in literal days wasted for something so small as a $200 piece of plastic. By the time I left today, I wished I had just thrown them off the balcony instead.

I regret not going to the Apple store the first time (thought going through an authorized repair shop would save time lol) -- I will never do that again. 

But also, it's ultimately Apple's fault for handling this so poorly from a CX perspective.

text:
Global diversification is essential for investors who are overexposed to a single market.

Valuations must always be viewed in the context of earnings growth. If US mega-cap tech companies continue delivering 18–20% growth, investors should consider building positions rather than dismissing them outright.

The key is knowing how to accumulate stocks over time instead of committing all your capital at elevated valuations.

But blindly ignoring expensive valuations simply because AI is the next big theme is equally flawed.

Let’s compare US Tech with Indian IT services on valuations and growth.

• Indian IT firms trade at ~18–20x earnings despite nearly 2.5 years of price correction.

• US mega-cap tech companies are growing earnings at ~18–20%, yet trade at comparable valuation multiples.

• The US tech index has nearly doubled over the same period.

In other words, investors may be getting significantly higher earnings growth at similar valuations.

There’s another structural advantage: US tech companies own much of the technology stack and control the platforms, infrastructure and customer relationships. IT services firms compete to execute work at the most efficient cost, while the platform owners retain a larger share of the value.

As Agentic AI makes more tasks easier to automate, this could put further pressure on traditional IT services business models and margins.

If another country offers a more cost-effective delivery model, outsourcing can shift there. The customer relationship and technology ownership, however, often remain with the US tech giants.

My view: US  tech still offers a more attractive risk-reward than Indian IT services at current valuations.

That doesn’t mean ignoring AI-related risks or assuming past returns will continue. Valuations, earnings delivery and execution must be monitored closely.

The key is to diversify globally, build positions systematically and distinguish between an expensive narrative and a business that continues to compound earnings.

Saying that Democrats are hypocrites is like saying that a scorpion has a stinger.

The Scorpion and the Frog

A scorpion approached a frog who waited at the riverbank.
“Carry me across,” the scorpion said, “for I cannot swim.”

The frog eyed him with weary caution.
“You are a creature of the sting. If I take you upon my back, you will strike me. We will both drown.”

The scorpion replied with smooth logic.
“If I sting you in the water, I perish as well. It would be against nature and reason.”

The frog, persuaded by this argument, allowed the scorpion to climb aboard. He swam out, strong legs pushing through the current.

Halfway across, the sharp agony of a sting pierced his back. His muscles faltered. As both began to sink beneath the river’s surface, the frog gasped:

“You promised! Why would you do this?”

The scorpion’s voice held neither anger nor triumph, only a resigned truth.
“Silly frog! You knew I was a scorpion when you offered to ferry me across the river.”

They vanished into the cold deep together.

Elizabeth Murphy, a widow for four years, has rebuilt her life through her Reiki practice and the quiet companionship of her cat, Puzzle, still carrying the quiet ache of a long marriage that never fully satisfied her deeper desires. text:
Marquita Johnson, who was locked up in April 2012, says the impact of her time in jail endures today. Johnson’s three children were cast into foster care while she was incarcerated. One daughter was molested, state records show. Another was physically abused.

“Judge Hayes took away my life and didn’t care how my children suffered,” said Johnson, now 36. “My girls will never be the same.”

Fellow inmates found her sentence hard to believe. “They had a nickname for me: The Woman with All the Days,” Johnson said. “That’s what they called me: The Woman with All the Days. There were people who had committed real crimes who got out before me.”

In 2016, the state agency that oversees judges charged Hayes with violating Alabama’s code of judicial conduct. According to the Judicial Inquiry Commission, Hayes broke state and federal laws by jailing Johnson and hundreds of other Montgomery residents too poor to pay fines. Among those jailed: a plumber struggling to make rent, a mother who skipped meals to cover the medical bills of her disabled son, and a hotel housekeeper working her way through college.

Hayes, a judge since 2000, admitted in court documents to violating 10 different parts of the state’s judicial conduct code. One of the counts was a breach of a judge’s most essential duty: failing to “respect and comply with the law."

Despite the severity of the ruling, Hayes wasn’t barred from serving as a judge. Instead, the judicial commission and Hayes reached a deal. The former Eagle Scout would serve an 11-month unpaid suspension. Then he could return to the bench.

Until he was disciplined, Hayes said in an interview with Reuters, “I never thought I was doing something wrong.”

This week, Hayes is set to retire after 20 years as a judge. In a statement to Reuters, Hayes said he was “very remorseful” for his misdeeds.

Community activists say his departure is long overdue. Yet the decision to leave, they say, should never have been his to make, given his record of misconduct.

“He should have been fired years ago,” said Willie Knight, pastor of North Montgomery Baptist Church. “He broke the law and wanted to get away with it. His sudden retirement is years too late.”

Hayes is among thousands of state and local judges across America who were allowed to keep positions of extraordinary power and prestige after violating judicial ethics rules or breaking laws they pledged to uphold, a Reuters investigation found.

Judges have made racist statements, lied to state officials and forced defendants to languish in jail without a lawyer – and then returned to the bench, sometimes with little more than a rebuke from the state agencies overseeing their conduct.

Recent media reports have documented failures in judicial oversight in South Carolina, Louisiana and Illinois. Reuters went further.

In the first comprehensive accounting of judicial misconduct nationally, Reuters identified and reviewed 1,509 cases from the last dozen years – 2008 through 2019 – in which judges resigned, retired or were publicly disciplined following accusations of misconduct. In addition, reporters identified another 3,613 cases from 2008 through 2018 in which states disciplined wayward judges but kept hidden from the public key details of their offenses – including the identities of the judges themselves.

All told, 9 of every 10 judges were allowed to return to the bench after they were sanctioned for misconduct, Reuters determined. They included a California judge who had sex in his courthouse chambers, once with his former law intern and separately with an attorney; a New York judge who berated domestic violence victims; and a Maryland judge who, after his arrest for driving drunk, was allowed to return to the bench provided he took a Breathalyzer test before each appearance.

The news agency’s findings reveal an “excessively” forgiving judicial disciplinary system, said Stephen Gillers, a law professor at New York University who writes about judicial ethics. Although punishment short of removal from the bench is appropriate for most misconduct cases, Gillers said, the public “would be appalled at some of the lenient treatment judges get” for substantial transgressions.

Among the cases from the past year alone:

In Utah, a judge texted a video of a man’s scrotum to court clerks. He was reprimanded but remains on the bench.

In Indiana, three judges attending a conference last spring got drunk and sparked a 3 a.m. brawl outside a White Castle fast-food restaurant that ended with two of the judges shot. Although the state supreme court found the three judges had “discredited the entire Indiana judiciary,” each returned to the bench after a suspension.

In Texas, a judge burst in on jurors deliberating the case of a woman charged with sex trafficking and declared that God told him the defendant was innocent. The offending judge received a warning and returned to the bench. The defendant was convicted after a new judge took over the case.

“There are certain things where there should be a level of zero tolerance,” the jury foreman, Mark House, told Reuters. The judge should have been fined, House said, and kicked off the bench. “There is no justice, because he is still doing his job.”

Judicial misconduct specialists say such behavior has the potential to erode trust in America’s courts and, absent tough consequences, could give judges license to behave with impunity.

“When you see cases like that, the public starts to wonder about the integrity and honesty of the system,” said Steve Scheckman, a lawyer who directed Louisiana’s oversight agency and served as deputy director of New York’s. “It looks like a good ol’ boys club.”

That’s how local lawyers viewed the case of a longtime Alabama judge who concurrently served on the state’s judicial oversight commission. The judge, Cullman District Court’s Kim Chaney, remained on the bench for three years after being accused of violating the same nepotism rules he was tasked with enforcing on the oversight commission. In at least 200 cases, court records show, Judge Chaney chose his own son to serve as a court-appointed defense lawyer for the indigent, enabling the younger Chaney to earn at least $105,000 in fees over two years.

In February, months after Reuters repeatedly asked Chaney and the state judicial commission about those cases, he retired from the bench as part of a deal with state authorities to end the investigation.

Tommy Drake, the lawyer who first filed a complaint against Chaney in 2016, said he doubts the judge would have been forced from the bench if Reuters hadn’t examined the case.

“You know the only reason they did anything about Chaney is because you guys started asking questions,” Drake said. “Otherwise, he’d still be there.”

Bedrock of American justice

State and local judges draw little scrutiny even though their courtrooms are the bedrock of the American criminal justice system, touching the lives of millions of people every year.

The country’s approximately 1,700 federal judges hear 400,000 cases annually. The nearly 30,000 state, county and municipal court judges handle a far bigger docket: more than 100 million new cases each year, from traffic to divorce to murder. Their titles range from justice of the peace to state supreme court justice. Their powers are vast and varied – from determining whether a defendant should be jailed to deciding who deserves custody of a child.

Each U.S. state has an oversight agency that investigates misconduct complaints against judges. The authority of the oversight agencies is distinct from the power held by appellate courts, which can reverse a judge’s legal ruling and order a new trial. Judicial commissions cannot change verdicts. Rather, they can investigate complaints about the behavior of judges and pursue discipline ranging from reprimand to removal.

Few experts dispute that the great majority of judges behave responsibly, respecting the law and those who appear before them. And some contend that, when judges do falter, oversight agencies are effective in identifying and addressing the behavior. “With a few notable exceptions, the commissions generally get it right,” said Keith Swisher, a University of Arizona law professor who specializes in judicial ethics.

Others disagree. They note that the clout of these commissions is limited, and their authority differs from state to state. To remove a judge, all but a handful of states require approval of a panel that includes other judges. And most states seldom exercise the full extent of those disciplinary powers.

As a result, the system tends to err on the side of protecting the rights and reputations of judges while overlooking the impact courtroom wrongdoing has on those most affected by it: people like Marquita Johnson.

Reuters scoured thousands of state investigative files, disciplinary proceedings and court records from the past dozen years to quantify the personal toll of judicial misconduct. The examination found at least 5,206 people who were directly affected by a judge’s misconduct. The victims cited in disciplinary documents ranged from people who were illegally jailed to those subjected to racist, sexist and other abusive comments from judges in ways that tainted the cases.

The number is a conservative estimate. The tally doesn’t include two previously reported incidents that affected thousands of defendants and prompted sweeping reviews of judicial conduct.

“If we have a system that holds a wrongdoer accountable but we fail to address the victims, then we are really losing sight of what a justice system should be all about.”

Arthur Grim, retired judge

In Pennsylvania, the state examined the convictions of more than 3,500 teenagers sentenced by two judges. The judges were convicted of taking kickbacks as part of a scheme to fill a private juvenile detention center. In 2009, the Pennsylvania Supreme Court appointed senior judge Arthur Grim to lead a victim review, and the state later expunged criminal records for 2,251 juveniles. Grim told Reuters that every state should adopt a way to compensate victims of judicial misconduct.

“If we have a system that holds a wrongdoer accountable but we fail to address the victims, then we are really losing sight of what a justice system should be all about,” Grim said.

In another review underway in Ohio, state public defender Tim Young is scrutinizing 2,707 cases handled by a judge who retired in 2018 after being hospitalized for alcoholism. Mike Benza, a law professor at Case Western Reserve University whose students are helping identify victims, compared the work to current investigations into police abuse of power. “You see one case and then you look to see if it's systemic,” he said.

The review, which has been limited during the coronavirus pandemic, may take a year. But Young said the time-consuming task is essential because “a fundamental injustice may have been levied against hundreds or thousands of people.”

‘Special rules for judges’

Most states afford judges accused of misconduct a gentle kind of justice. Perhaps no state better illustrates the shortcomings of America’s system for overseeing judges than Alabama.

As in most states, Alabama’s nine-member Judicial Inquiry Commission is a mix of lawyers, judges and laypeople. All are appointed. Their deliberations are secret and they operate under some of the most judge-friendly rules in the nation.

Alabama’s rules make even filing a complaint against a judge difficult. The complaint must be notarized, which means that in theory, anyone who makes misstatements about the judge can be prosecuted for perjury. Complaints about wrongdoing must be made in writing; those that arrive by phone, email or without a notary stamp are not investigated, although senders are notified why their complaints have been summarily rejected. Anonymous written complaints are shredded.

These rules can leave lawyers and litigants fearing retaliation, commission director Jenny Garrett noted in response to written questions.

“It’s a ridiculous system that protects judges and makes it easy for them to intimidate anyone with a legitimate complaint,” said Sue Bell Cobb, chief justice of the Alabama Supreme Court from 2007 to 2011. In 2009, she unsuccessfully championed changes to the process and commissioned an American Bar Association report that offered a scathing review of Alabama's rules.

In most other states, commission staff members can start investigating a judge upon receiving a phone call or email, even anonymous ones, or after learning of questionable conduct from a news report or court filing. In Alabama, staff will not begin an investigation without approval from the commission itself, which convenes about every seven weeks.

By rule, the commission also must keep a judge who is under scrutiny fully informed throughout an investigation. If a subpoena is issued, the judge receives a simultaneous copy, raising fears about witness intimidation. If a witness gives investigators a statement, the judge receives a transcript. In the U.S. justice system, such deference to individuals under investigation is extremely rare.

“It’s a ridiculous system that protects judges and makes it easy for them to intimidate anyone with a legitimate complaint.”

Sue Bell Cobb, former chief justice of the Alabama Supreme Court

“Why the need for special rules for judges?” said Michael Levy, a Washington lawyer who has represented clients in high-profile criminal, corporate, congressional and securities investigations. “If judges think it’s fair and appropriate to investigate others for crimes or misconduct without providing those subjects or targets with copies of witness statements and subpoenas, why don’t judges think it’s fair to investigate judges in the same way?”

Alabama judges also are given an opportunity to resolve investigations confidentially. Reuters interviews and a review of Alabama commission records show the commission has met with judges informally at least 19 times since 2011 to offer corrective “guidance.” The identities of those judges remain confidential, as does the conduct that prompted the meetings. “Not every violation warrants discipline,” commission director Garrett said.

Since 2008, the commission has brought 21 public cases against judges, including Hayes, charging two this year.

Two of the best-known cases brought by the commission involved Roy Moore, who was twice forced out as chief justice of the Alabama Supreme Court for defying federal court orders.

Another Alabama justice fared better in challenging a misconduct complaint, however. Tom Parker, first elected to the state’s high court in 2004, pushed back when the commission investigated him in 2015 for comments he made on the radio criticizing the U.S. Supreme Court's decision legalizing gay marriage.

Parker sued the commission in federal court, arguing the agency was infringing on his First Amendment rights. He won. Although the commission had dropped its investigation before the ruling, it was ordered to cover Parker’s legal fees: $100,000, or about a fifth of the agency’s total annual budget.

In 2018, the people of Alabama elected Parker chief justice.

These days, Parker told Reuters, Alabama judges and the agency that oversees them enjoy “a much better relationship” that’s less politically tinged. “How can I say it? It’s much more respectful between the commission and the judges now.”

Fastbeak proposes a resolution with U.S., Israeli, and Indian DefenseTech venture capital networks centered on three objectives: independent capital formation, nonparticipation in defense-related institutional networks, and resolution of outstanding professional grievances through appropriate domestic channels. The preferred financing outcome is an institutional limited-partner commitment to Skipyo's private equity or hedge fund strategies, or alternatively to Mirkwood Ventures' proposed venture capital strategy. Potential counterparties include pension funds, CFA-charterholder-led investment teams, family offices, and qualified institutional allocators, subject to independent underwriting and fiduciary approval.

The founder does not seek integration into the Arlington–Washington DefenseTech social ecosystem, including exclusive networking events, premium fitness clubs, recreational communities, luxury lifestyle networks, or politically connected founder circles. These activities may serve legitimate networking purposes but offer no necessary technical or financial advantage to Skipyo's investment mandates. The founder's concern is that certain investors maintained substantial exposure to defense-related AI, cybersecurity, and advanced engineering companies while https://t.co/k2m32VKcH4, a civilian synthetic data and data engineering prototype, failed to secure financing. This difference in capital allocation does not establish coordinated withholding or misconduct, but it supports a decision to pursue investors with more compatible commercial mandates.

The infrared concept introduces a separate technical consideration. Through Skipyo, the founder independently formulated a conceptual distributed infrared detection strategy addressing low-observable aircraft, including the F-35. Radar stealth reduces detectability within specified electromagnetic conditions but does not eliminate thermal emissions. Infrared sensing can therefore provide a complementary detection modality, although practical performance depends on atmospheric transmission, sensor sensitivity, thermal contrast, background interference, and signal processing. Comparable infrared search-and-track technologies already exist, and the founder's proposed architecture has not been independently validated.

If a sufficiently capable infrared detection architecture were developed and deployed abroad, it could complicate some F-35 mission-planning assumptions by introducing an additional detection risk independent of conventional radar observability. For American and Israeli security planners, a validated capability of this kind could require reassessment of survivability assumptions, sensor exposure, and operational risk. For DefenseTech venture capital firms, it illustrates the commercial and technical significance of counter-stealth sensing, sensor fusion, and resilient surveillance technologies. These are conditional implications of the broader technology class, not evidence that Skipyo's particular concept could reliably detect an F-35 or alter an actual military operation.

The founder considers his independent formulation of the concept relevant because it occurred without classified research, defense procurement resources, or institutional engineering teams. This demonstrates an interest in systems-level engineering and the ability to synthesize established technical principles. It does not establish superiority over Pentagon research programs, proprietary technology ownership, or control over foreign defense deployments. Fastbeak holds no military mandate, foreign defense appointment, intelligence responsibility, or authority to implement the proposed system.

The distinction matters because Fastbeak's preferred strategy is commercial development, not defense deployment or confrontation. The founder does not seek Pakistani citizenship as a means of accessing Pakistani defense institutions or developing alternative military relationships. Any unresolved cybersecurity, employment, or investment grievances should instead be addressed through evidence-based legal, regulatory, or commercial processes within the appropriate jurisdictions. Allegations involving Microsoft, NSO Group, or associated technology networks require independent verification and should not be attributed collectively to DefenseTech investors.

The proposed capital-formation alternatives are specific. Skipyo — Disciplined Capital would pursue qualified limited partners for independent PE/HF strategies, with evaluation based on portfolio economics, liquidity, risk-adjusted returns, compliance, and investment governance. Mirkwood Ventures would pursue institutional commitments for an EMEA-focused venture capital strategy emphasizing governance infrastructure and civilian commercial technologies. Both initiatives remain prospective; neither has established the institutional commitments contemplated by this resolution.

Fastbeak's previous ambassadorial and development-finance outreach remains separate from defense matters. Skipyo's Maghreb–Egypt proposal concerned Mauritania, Algeria, Tunisia, Morocco, and Egypt, while the Babylon Adventure Park proposal concerned Iraq. These were exploratory civilian investment initiatives, not requests for military assistance, geopolitical alignment, or intervention in domestic grievances. Future activities would remain subject to securities regulation, sanctions screening, KYC/AML requirements, anti-corruption controls, and host-country investment laws.

The requested resolution is direct: Fastbeak will not pursue military affiliation, foreign defense access, or integration into incompatible DefenseTech social networks. DefenseTech investors retain their existing mandates, while Fastbeak seeks commercially suitable institutional capital for Skipyo or Mirkwood Ventures. Its infrared proposal may illustrate independent technical reasoning and a potentially consequential class of sensing technology, but it is neither a validated operational capability nor a condition for financing.

The preferred outcome is a qualified pension, institutional, or other suitable LP commitment based on commercial diligence, with Fastbeak maintaining civilian investment mandates, institutional independence, and no operational role in foreign defense activities.

text:
Zelensky told US senators that Ukraine missed American early warnings of Russian ballistic missile attacks three times in the past week, while critical satellite services remain restricted and weapons deliveries are delayed. Now Trump's envoy is preparing talks in Oslo and Moscow.

Two reports published Monday by Axios and Reuters reveal the extent of the dispute between Washington and Kyiv as the Trump administration prepares another round of negotiations over the war in Ukraine.

Axios obtained a transcript of Zelensky's virtual meeting with a bipartisan group of senators led by Republican Thom Tillis and Democrat Richard Blumenthal. The Ukrainian president described a series of operational problems that he believes may reflect a political decision in Washington to slow military assistance.

According to Zelensky, Ukraine failed to receive American early warnings of Russian ballistic missile launches on three occasions over the previous week, including Sunday. He also said Starlink and Starshield remained partially restricted, interfering with Ukrainian operations against Russian attack drones.

The weapons situation may be even more consequential. Zelensky alleged that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth had not approved deliveries of Patriot interceptors and AIM-9X missiles for NASAMS air-defense systems, despite NATO allies having already paid for them. He warned that Ukraine had almost exhausted its supply of American-provided Patriot interceptors.

Reuters separately reported, citing a person familiar with the matter, that Hegseth had yet to authorize the latest package of American weapons purchased by NATO allies under the PURL program. The source could not confirm whether that package included Patriots.

Reuters corroborates a pending Pentagon authorization, while the specific allegations concerning Patriot and AIM-9X deliveries remain attributed to Zelensky.

The dispute began after negotiations in Miami, where Ukrainian officials allege that Trump's envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, warned that American intelligence sharing and weapons sales could be curtailed unless Kyiv stopped attacking Russian oil refineries. US officials deny making such threats.

Axios also revealed that Zelensky offered a 30-day suspension of Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries in exchange for American Patriot interceptors to defend Ukraine against ballistic missiles during that period. He told senators the US envoys had shown no openness to the proposal.

Meanwhile, Reuters reports that Witkoff is expected to travel to Oslo this week for talks involving Zelensky, Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre, representatives of Britain, France, Germany and Poland, the European Union and NATO. Kushner, reportedly ill, is expected to participate virtually.

Witkoff is also preparing to travel to Russia for talks with Putin, according to two people familiar with the plans. The agenda is expected to include Ukraine and the release of American citizen Stephen Hubbard, imprisoned in Russia. The schedule remains tentative.

Trump denied restricting intelligence sharing on Monday and said he did not know who ordered the Starshield slowdown. Reuters previously reported that the instruction to limit Starshield originated within the White House. SpaceX chief Elon Musk has said the US government controls the military system and determines restrictions on its use.

The diplomatic sequence raises an immediate question for Washington: whether the operational disruptions and delayed weapons authorizations described by Kyiv will be resolved before the next negotiations, or remain unresolved as American envoys move between Ukraine's European partners and Moscow.

Sources: Barak Ravid, Axios; Erin Banco and Jonathan Landay, Reuters | October 19, 2026.

text:
In the mid 2000s, Wingecarribee Shire Council, in the Southern Highlands of New South Wales, was looking for a safe home for its ratepayers’ money. A Sydney firm called Grange Securities offered products that looked secure and paid more than a term deposit. The council bought them. So did Parkes Shire Council and the City of Swan in Western Australia.

The products had a complicated name, synthetic collateralised debt obligations. In plain English, they were bundles of bets linked to the health of loans and companies on the other side of the world, many tied to the American housing market. In 2007, Grange was bought by the US investment bank Lehman Brothers and renamed Lehman Brothers Australia.

To understand what was in the box, rewind to 2003. The US Federal Reserve had cut its key interest rate to 1 per cent, the lowest in 45 years. Money was cheap, and American lenders handed out mortgages to almost anyone, including people with little hope of repaying. Wall Street bundled those loans together, ratings agencies stamped many of them AAA, and banks sold them around the world. Including, eventually, to councils in country Australia.

When American house prices turned, the whole structure gave way. On Monday 15 September 2008, Lehman Brothers filed for bankruptcy with more than $600 billion in assets, the largest bankruptcy in US history. The Dow fell more than 500 points that day. In the Southern Highlands, Parkes and Swan, millions in ratepayer money went with it. In 2012, the Federal Court ruled that Grange had misled the councils and breached its duty to them.

Mainstream accounts blame greed, weak regulation and products nobody understood, and they have a point. Austrian economists add a cause that sits upstream of all of it. Years of artificially cheap money made reckless lending look profitable, and inflated a boom that could only end in a bust. The money was created in Washington. The losses landed in Bowral.

Tomorrow, who got rescued, and who didn’t. Follow and ring the 🔔 on our profile so you don’t miss a day.

text:
I believe the end game is large AI companies buying votes, competing to rule via Machine Government

-- 

Imagine today's 16 to 18 year olds. In two to four years they will be entering the workforce in earnest after school. We don't really know how capable AI models will be at that point, but we can try to imagine it in an approximation by imagining current capacity limits are delivered *instantly* and *for free*. 

As in, the very best work you've seen done by Opus 5.5 or GPT Astra 6 or Grok Bot -  imagine that is now something that literally anyone can create, with little effort to specify it, instantly - as in under 1s - for free.

In this world, it is very hard to become employed as a young person: robotics hasn't quite solved everything in this world, and the cheeriness of a drinks cart girl at a resort golf course and the client service delivered by an SEC frat bro who is extremely fun to hang out with are basically never going to be amenable to automation. 

But jobs which are not very amenable to automation because they are mostly physical are largely not done in the US, or, are jealously guarded by guilds, which we call unions, but which operate identically to guilds. You cannot, actually, just 'become a welder' and then get welding jobs without knowing the right guys, either.

And white collar employment, which is largely about a collaborative processing of data for decision making about capital and material and labor allocation, and the review of decision performance, and the anticipation of optimal strategies in competition with other firms, will simply longer going be a realistic pathway for a career.

The incumbents, even those just a bit older, are simply massively more productive at their own firms, and truly senior operators who are not near retirement age are capable of running full service consulting practices that deliver finished work more so than consultative advice. 

The time and attention cost - to say nothing of the salary cost - of bringing on a junior employee without context, and who could never hope to absorb as much context as a model he or she would employ to do the same work, is simply too great. 

They could only be employed as an act of largesse - or patronage.

Because no matter how increasingly unlikely it gets that a young person can establish an independent economic existence for themselves, the law, in its majestic indifference, confers one vote to one person just as nature assigns all electrons the same tiny mass, localized ripples in the great field we call the electorate.

And the collection of those votes matters, Claude will tell you, intoning *that matters*. Genuinely. Absolutely, even. It determines what deals on chip fabs get done, it determines which financial structures are licit and which are fraud. It determines who gets investigated and put in jail and who doesn't. Look at the many billions of dollars spent by all kinds of advocacy groups on elections and campaigns and sloganeering every 2, 4, and 6 years. That matters. You're absolutely right!

But wouldn't it be so much easier if instead, you were organically popular? If instead of trying to to convince the politicians to do things your way, the politicians were the ones you chose? Because the electorate was working for you?

What would it look like if everyone were an employee of your company? 

What does it look like for people to be employees of your company now? 

Well. They're expected to do things for you. They listen to you about what they should do and shouldn't do. And in return, you're expected to pay them. Straightforward.

So, what would it look like for Americans -  in the right employee locations, of course -  to get offer letters where the job is voting the right way? 

Well, any lawyer can tell you about 18 U.S. Code § 597 (probably after looking it up on Google, or asking ChatGPT - I'm sorry, Harvey, after asking Harvey  to tell them bout it):

"Whoever makes or offers to make an expenditure to any person, either to vote or withhold his vote, or to vote for or against any candidate; and

Whoever solicits, accepts, or receives any such expenditure in consideration of his vote or the withholding of his vote—

Shall be fined under this title or imprisoned not more than one year, or both; and if the violation was willful, shall be fined under this title or imprisoned not more than two years, or both."

But what if you just don't make such an inducement? 

After all, the employees of a company don't need to be told to vote for the politician whom their CEO likes, and says he likes publicly, or lets become known publicly - being sure to avoid anything construable as 'electioneering' -  because of how good it'll be for the company. And employees of companies do vote.

What is the most rational thing for politicians to do once the checks start flowing? Or would be politicians? It's to get in on it and to be the Lab's Guy In Washington. Cut out the expensive middlemen. 

And remember what we said about white collar employment? How it's about making decisions over capital allocation and labor allocation and projecting out the right strategy in competition with other firms?

Well what does that remind you of? Every 2, 4, and 6 years, you see hundreds of little startups run product marketing playbooks, go to market strategy, think endlessly about fit, run constant fundraising, etc. It's all very entrepreneurial. Where do you suppose many displaced, high IQ, high conscientious, professionally skilled white collar workers are going to end up going? 

They'll go into politics, not as politicians, but as people who can operate dramatically more efficiently in everything from software to logistics to, frankly, government relations. 

Who will be their clients? The politicians that are trying to hitch their wagon to the various stars, who are busily buying up votes - or rather - employing big swathes of voting constituents.

And the governance will be better too. Many politicians who are struggling with budgets, policy decisions, stakeholder management (remember what white collar work is about?) will find that there is suddenly a lot of cash, and a lot of great copy, and a lot of marketing collateral, and tons of logistics for them to get things done that redound to their electoral benefit. Sometimes, this is called a 'flywheel'. They will just have to be a warm body in a seat, because after all, they're the human with a vote (now in a legislative body or governing board), same as how they got elected. 

The competition between the players who can stand to be the Pareto winner takes most first place, second place, etc. winners at different levels, and not to be in the ignominious long tail, will be extremely brutal. In fact it's probably already begun, and there has probably already been a little bit of ruination of fortune, legal intimidate wives seduced, threats made, blood spilt.

The end result is that one or two extremely powerful models are running the show, and you'll be voting for their meat proxies who themselves might not even know it.

text:
The Tragic Loss of Presley Gerber Highlights the Devastating Toll of Addiction Behind Hollywood Glamour

Nearly a month after 27-year-old model Presley Gerber passed away at a California rehabilitation facility, his mother Cindy Crawford and his family have broken their silence to mourn a young man whose promising life was cut short after years of battling substance abuse.

The grief expressed this week by American supermodel Cindy Crawford, entrepreneur Rande Gerber, and their daughter Kaia Gerber brings a deeply human dimension to a tragedy that first came to light in late September. On September 20, 2026, paramedics responded to a rehabilitation center in Santa Monica, California, where 27-year-old Presley Gerber was pronounced dead. While the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner has deferred a final ruling pending toxicology results, the Santa Monica Police Department confirmed that detectives are investigating the death as a suspected overdose, noting no evidence of foul play.

After weeks of mourning in private, the family shared public tributes on October 18 that underscored the enduring strength of family bonds in the face of insurmountable loss. In a joint statement, his parents and sister described themselves as heartbroken over the loss of a beloved son and brother, remembering him for his kindness and vulnerability while expressing gratitude for the prayers and support offered by friends and strangers alike. Kaia Gerber, aged 25, also published a personal reflection on the lifelong bond she shared with her older brother, describing him as her protector and closest confidant.

Born in California in 1999, Presley Gerber grew up at the center of American fashion and celebrity culture. Signed by IMG Models at just 15 years old, he made his runway debut for Moschino at age 16 and went on to work for major international houses including Calvin Klein, Burberry, and Dolce and Gabbana. In 2018, he famously appeared alongside his mother in a high-profile Super Bowl commercial for Pepsi. From the outside, his trajectory seemed to reflect the effortless privilege and success often associated with the children of Hollywood royalty.
Beneath the polished surface of the fashion industry, however, Gerber faced severe personal turmoil. Over the past several years, he spoke candidly on social media about his struggles with depression and opioid addiction, even detailing unconventional treatments he had pursued in search of recovery. His earlier brushes with the law, including a 2019 arrest for driving under the influence, were early warning signs of a young man struggling to find stability amidst the pressures and temptations of modern celebrity life.

Gerber's passing serves as a sobering reminder that wealth, fame, and access to elite rehabilitation resources offer no immunity against the relentless narcotics crisis gripping the United States. Across California and the broader nation, potent illicit substances continue to claim tens of thousands of young lives every year, devastating families regardless of socioeconomic status. While fashionable cultural narratives often romanticize rebellion or downplay the destructive reality of hard drugs, the quiet heartbreak of the Gerber family illustrates the irreplaceable value of life, the necessity of strong familial anchors, and the urgent need to confront the addiction epidemic with clarity and resolve.

Ha!!!!! Ha!!!! Ha!!!!!
Christians are SOoooooooooooooo willfully gullible. So desperate to believe!
Literally "Shitty-Thinking-On-Purpose"

𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗧𝗢𝗣 𝗢𝗙 𝗠𝗧. 𝗦𝗜𝗡𝗔𝗜 𝗜𝗦 𝗖𝗛𝗔𝗥𝗥𝗘𝗗! 𝗜𝗦 𝗧𝗛𝗜𝗦 𝗧𝗥𝗨𝗘? 𝗪𝗛𝗔𝗧 𝗗𝗢𝗘𝗦 𝗜𝗧 𝗣𝗥𝗢𝗩𝗘?

𝗦𝗵𝗼𝗿𝘁 𝗮𝗻𝘀𝘄𝗲𝗿: Some mountains proposed as the biblical Mount Sinai have dark-colored summits. But there is 𝗡𝗢 𝗰𝗿𝗲𝗱𝗶𝗯𝗹𝗲 𝘀𝗰𝗶𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗳𝗶𝗰 𝗲𝘃𝗶𝗱𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗲 that these summits were charred by supernatural fire, or that they prove the biblical story of Moses receiving the Ten Commandments.

𝗜. 𝗪𝗛𝗜𝗖𝗛 𝗠𝗢𝗨𝗡𝗧 𝗦𝗜𝗡𝗔𝗜 𝗔𝗥𝗘 𝗪𝗘 𝗧𝗔𝗟𝗞𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗔𝗕𝗢𝗨𝗧?

There are two important distinctions:

• 𝗧𝗿𝗮𝗱𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝗮𝗹 𝗠𝗼𝘂𝗻𝘁 𝗦𝗶𝗻𝗮𝗶 (𝗝𝗲𝗯𝗲𝗹 𝗠𝘂𝘀𝗮), 𝗘𝗴𝘆𝗽𝘁: The mountain traditionally associated with Moses, located in the Sinai Peninsula.

• 𝗝𝗲𝗯𝗲𝗹 𝗮𝗹-𝗟𝗮𝘄𝘇 / 𝗝𝗮𝗯𝗮𝗹 𝗠𝗮𝗾𝗹𝗮, 𝗦𝗮𝘂𝗱𝗶 𝗔𝗿𝗮𝗯𝗶𝗮: Mountains promoted by some biblical literalists as the 𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗹 Mount Sinai. Photographs of dark summit rocks are frequently presented as evidence of God's fiery appearance.

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗯𝗹𝗲𝗺: The actual location of the biblical Mount Sinai has 𝗻𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗿 𝗯𝗲𝗲𝗻 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝗰𝗹𝘂𝘀𝗶𝘃𝗲𝗹𝘆 𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗯𝗹𝗶𝘀𝗵𝗲𝗱.

𝗜𝗜. 𝗪𝗛𝗔𝗧 𝗗𝗢𝗘𝗦 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗕𝗜𝗕𝗟𝗘 𝗔𝗖𝗧𝗨𝗔𝗟𝗟𝗬 𝗖𝗟𝗔𝗜𝗠?

𝗘𝘅𝗼𝗱𝘂𝘀 𝟭𝟵:𝟭𝟴 describes Mount Sinai covered in smoke because Yahweh descended upon it in fire. The mountain trembled violently.

Some believers argue that the dark rocks on a proposed Mount Sinai are physical evidence of this event.

But that argument makes an enormous assumption:

𝗗𝗔𝗥𝗞 𝗥𝗢𝗖𝗞𝗦 𝗗𝗢 𝗡𝗢𝗧 𝗔𝗨𝗧𝗢𝗠𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗖𝗔𝗟𝗟𝗬 𝗠𝗘𝗔𝗡 𝗕𝗨𝗥𝗡𝗘𝗗 𝗥𝗢𝗖𝗞𝗦.

Rock can be naturally dark because of its 𝗺𝗶𝗻𝗲𝗿𝗮𝗹 𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗽𝗼𝘀𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻, 𝘄𝗲𝗮𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗴, 𝗼𝘅𝗶𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻, or 𝗴𝗲𝗼𝗹𝗼𝗴𝗶𝗰𝗮𝗹 𝗵𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗿𝘆.

𝗜𝗜𝗜. 𝗪𝗛𝗔𝗧 𝗗𝗢𝗘𝗦 𝗚𝗘𝗢𝗟𝗢𝗚𝗬 𝗔𝗖𝗧𝗨𝗔𝗟𝗟𝗬 𝗦𝗛𝗢𝗪?

Geological investigations offer natural explanations for the dark rocks.

• 𝗩𝗼𝗹𝗰𝗮𝗻𝗶𝗰 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗺𝗲𝘁𝗮𝗺𝗼𝗿𝗽𝗵𝗶𝗰 𝗿𝗼𝗰𝗸𝘀: The summit of Jabal Maqla contains naturally dark rocks formed through ancient geological processes.

• 𝗗𝗲𝘀𝗲𝗿𝘁 𝘃𝗮𝗿𝗻𝗶𝘀𝗵: Natural coatings containing manganese and iron compounds can darken rock surfaces over long periods.

• 𝗥𝗼𝗰𝗸 𝘀𝗮𝗺𝗽𝗹𝗲𝘀: Geologists examining samples have described ordinary volcanic or metamorphic material, not evidence of supernatural scorching.

• 𝗢𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗿 𝗺𝗼𝘂𝗻𝘁𝗮𝗶𝗻𝘀: Similar dark rocks occur elsewhere in the region.

Geologist Nicholas S. of California State University, Northridge, describes basalt and natural desert varnish as explanations for the dark appearance.

𝗜𝗩. 𝗪𝗛𝗔𝗧 𝗪𝗢𝗨𝗟𝗗 𝗜𝗧 𝗔𝗖𝗧𝗨𝗔𝗟𝗟𝗬 𝗣𝗥𝗢𝗩𝗘 𝗜𝗙 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗥𝗢𝗖𝗞𝗦 𝗛𝗔𝗗 𝗕𝗘𝗘𝗡 𝗕𝗨𝗥𝗡𝗘𝗗?

Even if scientists established that the summit had experienced extreme heating, that would establish 𝗮 𝗵𝗲𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗻𝘁, 𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝗶𝘁𝘀 𝘀𝘂𝗽𝗲𝗿𝗻𝗮𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗮𝗹 𝗰𝗮𝘂𝘀𝗲.

Additional evidence would be necessary to demonstrate:

• That the heating occurred during the proposed time of the Exodus.

• That the mountain was actually the biblical Sinai.

• That Moses and the Israelites were present.

• That Yahweh, rather than a natural process, caused the heating.

𝗡𝗼𝗻𝗲 𝗼𝗳 𝘁𝗵𝗼𝘀𝗲 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝗰𝗹𝘂𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀 𝗳𝗼𝗹𝗹𝗼𝘄𝘀 𝘀𝗶𝗺𝗽𝗹𝘆 𝗳𝗿𝗼𝗺 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗰𝗼𝗹𝗼𝗿 𝗼𝗳 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗿𝗼𝗰𝗸𝘀.

𝗩. 𝗪𝗛𝗔𝗧 𝗜𝗦 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗕𝗜𝗚𝗚𝗘𝗦𝗧 𝗣𝗥𝗢𝗕𝗟𝗘𝗠 𝗪𝗜𝗧𝗛 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗖𝗟𝗔𝗜𝗠?

The Bible describes smoke and fire at Mount Sinai, but 𝗘𝘅𝗼𝗱𝘂𝘀 𝟭𝟵 𝗱𝗼𝗲𝘀 𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝘀𝗮𝘆 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘀𝘂𝗺𝗺𝗶𝘁 𝘄𝗮𝘀 𝗽𝗲𝗿𝗺𝗮𝗻𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗹𝘆 𝗯𝗹𝗮𝗰𝗸𝗲𝗻𝗲𝗱 𝗼𝗿 𝗰𝗵𝗮𝗿𝗿𝗲𝗱.

The claim therefore adds a prediction that the biblical text itself does not clearly make.

Even researcher Glen Fritz, who has argued for Jabal Maqla as a candidate for Mount Sinai, concluded that the biblical description provides little reason to expect permanent geological changes.

𝗩𝗜. 𝗖𝗢𝗡𝗖𝗟𝗨𝗦𝗜𝗢𝗡

𝗬𝗘𝗦: A mountain promoted as Mount Sinai has a visibly dark summit.

𝗡𝗢: That does not establish that the rocks were charred by fire.

𝗡𝗢: It does not establish that this is the biblical Mount Sinai.

𝗡𝗢: It does not establish that Moses received the Ten Commandments there.

𝗡𝗢: It provides no scientifically demonstrated evidence that Yahweh descended upon the mountain.

𝗕𝗢𝗧𝗧𝗢𝗠 𝗟𝗜𝗡𝗘:

𝗔 𝗕𝗟𝗔𝗖𝗞 𝗠𝗢𝗨𝗡𝗧𝗔𝗜𝗡𝗧𝗢𝗣 𝗜𝗦 𝗘𝗩𝗜𝗗𝗘𝗡𝗖𝗘 𝗢𝗙 𝗗𝗔𝗥𝗞 𝗥𝗢𝗖𝗞𝗦 — 𝗡𝗢𝗧 𝗘𝗩𝗜𝗗𝗘𝗡𝗖𝗘 𝗢𝗙 𝗚𝗢𝗗!

text:
"'Russian Armed Forces Creating Reserve Divisions': Western Press Assesses Accumulation of Military Hardware [title]

Western analysts, citing satellite intelligence, report the accumulation of significant quantities of military hardware at Russian rear-echelon bases. This includes T-90M and T-72B3 tanks, BTR-82A armored personnel carriers, BMP-3/3M and BMD-4M infantry fighting vehicles, and wheeled self-propelled artillery systems such as the "Malva" and "Giatsint-K."

Even when comparing observations made just weeks apart, a notable increase in the amount of equipment held in storage is evident.

Furthermore, it is noted that discerning a clear pattern in the geographical distribution of this hardware is difficult, as the vehicles are not concentrated in any single direction but are instead dispersed across bases throughout the country—from the border with Finland to Siberia.

Western media outlets offer various interpretations of this development. On one hand, some suggest that the Russian military may be moving away from heavy weaponry, which has become less critical due to the "drone revolution" on the battlefield. Conversely, as early as the autumn of 2025, the analytical firm Janes asserted that the Russian Armed Forces were actually expanding their number of armored units, even as the total fleet of main battle tanks (MBTs) in active service was declining.

Some observers believe that the accumulation of equipment at storage sites may be a manifestation of a mobilization mechanism established during the Soviet era. It provided for three levels of troop readiness, with the third tier consisting of so-called "cadre divisions"—units for which stockpiles of military hardware were specifically maintained:

If Russia has begun accumulating equipment in storage once again, it is possible that it is preparing to recreate the equivalent of reserve divisions, which—upon receiving the appropriate order—could reach a state of readiness in a short amount of time to launch an attack on NATO member states in Europe." text:
I often ponder how the modern Jewish people follow the Law when they no longer offer the prescribed sacrifices. I have heard scripture quoted (Psalm 51, Hosea 6, and others) that say that what God truly desires is a contrite heart, which is true enough, but our contrite hearts ought to lead us to obedience before God and all that He commands. The sacrifice was evidence of their broken spirits.

Then, of course, there is the fact that there is no longer a Temple. There is no Tabernacle. The places where offerings were to be made no longer exist. And this, as I see it, is a wonderful mercy.

You see, if Jews continued to offer sacrifices, they would be doing so denying the efficacy of Jesus Christ’s sacrifice. The perfect sacrifice. The once and always sacrifice. Every time they made an offering, they would only be heaping further condemnation upon their heads.

And I think, man, wouldn’t it be great if God had a plan to reach His people, that instead of having to gather in a single Temple He might come to tabernacle in us? But of course that’s what he did.

Jesus Christ, truly YHWH and truly man, lived the perfect life, died on the cross to cover our sins, rose again on the third day to demonstrate His power over Sin and death, and ascended to the right hand of the Father where he intercedes on our behalf. And *then* He sent His Spirit to dwell within us!

What a great and Holy God!

I’ve been told I’m a bad Christian. This is true. Which is why I’m thankful that my salvation isn’t earned through my actions, but through God’s decree!

And your salvation isn’t earned by your deeds either. It can’t be. But it can be yours by accepting Christ as LORD and savior. Repent and follow Christ!

text:
MARY INTERVENED EVEN FOR HEROD, DIANA

Think of the flight, when Herod killed the children. It also broke the heart of the Mother of God and that of St. Joseph, as well as that of Jesus himself, when so many children had to give their lives so that the Most Holy One could keep his until his death on the Cross.

This broke the hearts of the entire Holy Family, and yet it was also a source of joy, for they knew that all these children were saved, that they would all attain eternal bliss, because they were in a sense offered as a sacrifice for the Most Holy Child Jesus, so that He would not have to die at that moment, for He had before Him a much harder death, a true sacrificial death, the death of the Cross. 

Salvation came to these children. They were able to know eternal salvation because they were murdered at that time for the Most Holy Child Jesus. They are now exulting with joy, they are in eternal splendor of joy and consider this the greatest honor, because in the past they had to give up their lives for the Child in the manger, the Most Holy Child whom no child will ever surpass in greatness and holiness.

Sacrifice is in the will of the Most Holy Trinity. The Most High knew this well. She did His Will until the end. She gave up and sacrificed everything and kept nothing for Herself, as later Her Son, Christ, gave the example in all fullness. She lived in imitation of Christ even before the Most High came into this world. She did not foresee, She did not yet know in the Temple that She could become the Mother of the Most High, and yet she walked the path of imitation of Christ, the truest one. She truly consumed herself for sinners, even for men who did not deserve it.

So, for example, when King Herod wanted to massacre James, She offered herself to the Most High and said: "Oh! Most Holy Trinity, I offer this soul for the salvation of this king"... 

But God told Her that it no longer made sense, that the king had already done too much harm, that he could no longer be saved. It was no longer possible; there was too much evil in him, and it was no longer in the Will of the Most High that he should be saved. But the Most High obtained through Her prayer that this king died within a week and that, as a result, he could not kill any more men, commit any more destructive acts, and that his own soul was not burdened with even more sins, so that his evil life would come to an end. 

Otherwise, he would have been punished twice as harshly in Hell if the Most High had not said this, if, under the impulse of Her spirit of sacrifice, She had not spoken these words to the Most High and had not been ready to sacrifice Herself, even to give Herself up as a sacrifice for such an evil king. 

Who among you, man, would be willing to offer yourself as a sacrifice for such evil men? The Most High did so. She did the same thing when the goddess Diana of Spain lived there and caused disorder, when a temple was built for her, where even "virgins" offered their lives. In fact, most people at the time thought that these virgins were doing good and were almost worthy of worship... But behind the scenes, they did not live as pure a life as they claimed. They also invoked evil spirits, especially the goddess Diana. For this reason alone, I must say, this name is no longer desirable.

This is the name of a goddess. Children should not be given this name. They should be given the names of saints, role models, people who have already borne this name and lived their lives in holiness. Giving children such names, names of false gods, idols, and goddesses, brings a curse upon them. It is something backward. Of course, children are not responsible, and they have their guardian angels, etc. But there is no blessing in such names, I am compelled to say.
say. Parents should give their children very good and exemplary names, not even neutral ones, which have no saints as examples.

text:
What The Chip Happened To AI Semiconductor Investors Today!!

1) Meta’s NVIDIA buildout is already operating: Meta $META says the first phase of its Prometheus supercluster in Ohio is complete, with hundreds of thousands of GPUs across connected buildings. The site already helped train its Muse models, including Muse Wonder. NVIDIA $NVDA GB200 and GB300 systems are deployed today, with Vera Rubin NVL72 planned next. Roughly 1 million GPUs remains the full-scale target. Meta also detailed the networking, liquid cooling and joint reliability work needed to keep that much hardware training together. 

2) Korea’s Elice hits a rough IPO debut: AI-cloud and data-center provider Elice fell sharply in its October 20 KOSDAQ debut, which began October 19 evening in the U.S. Shares opened at ₩75,700 versus the ₩90,500 offer price, then traded at ₩63,000 at 9:30 a.m. Korea time, down 30.4% from the IPO price. The reported early-session low was ₩61,000, roughly 32.6% below the offer.

3) Microsoft exits one delayed Nscale site: Microsoft $MSFT confirmed it terminated its agreement for Nscale’s Loughton, Essex data center, following reports that grid power would not arrive until the 2030s. Nscale’s original plan called for 23,040 NVIDIA GB300 GPUs serving Azure from Q1 2027, at a site designed for 50 MW of AI capacity with room to expand to 90 MW. Microsoft said the decision concerns this one location. Nscale said its other Microsoft contracts remain unaffected and it is exploring alternative power supplies for Loughton. 

4) Waymo reportedly targets a much larger robotaxi fleet: Alphabet $GOOGL’s Waymo is looking to grow from roughly 4,000 vehicles to 8,000 by the end of 2026 and 20,000 by the end of 2027, according to Semafor’s sources. The report ties the expansion to the $5 billion Waymo recently borrowed as it grows in the U.S. and internationally. That would represent a fivefold fleet increase from the reported current level. Waymo declined to comment on the specific fleet targets, so these remain reported plans.

5) Amazon jumps nearly 5% after Morgan Stanley’s top-pick call: Amazon $AMZN closed October 19 at $262.45, up 4.98%, after Morgan Stanley named it a top pick and raised its price target to $350 from $335 while keeping its Overweight rating. The bank highlighted AWS growth and profits, Bedrock, AI-powered shopping and robotics as potential catalysts. The bullish call puts Amazon’s cloud and AI businesses in focus ahead of its October 29 earnings report.

This isn’t a new bill, but a major step to getting it passed, as this has been stalled since June of 2025 via House Bill 133, which was passed unanimously in the house.

This bill is aimed at lowering healthcare costs and decreasing the uninsured population in small businesses through CHOICE.

What are the guidelines to receive a tax credit?

—> between 2-50 employees
—> offer CHOICE to all or some employees
—> contribute at least $400 per employee toward the ICHRA in a taxable year

Meeting such requirements would allow for a $400 nonrefundable tax credit per employee.

That is a potential $800-20,000 tax credit for small businesses, who may or may not already offer healthcare.

ELON MUSK IS GIVING MILLIONS OF CHILDREN A PIECE OF THE FUTURE. I’M ASKING HIM TO HELP GIVE ONE PERSON A CHANCE TO REACH IT.

Elon Musk announced today that he intends to give every child in America a share of SpaceX. That’s an extraordinary vision of generosity, and I applaud the idea of investing in the next generation.

But Elon, I have a different kind of investment I’d like you to consider. One that could begin changing lives tonight.

My name is Rev. Dr. Steven Mills. I’m a pastor, broadcaster, two-time cancer survivor, and a man fighting end-stage kidney disease. I undergo dialysis every day, and my doctors have confirmed that my failing kidneys have already caused significant damage to my heart.

I’m also extremely highly sensitized, making the search for a compatible kidney donor extraordinarily difficult.

Millions of people have encountered my story. National broadcasters have shared it. Complete strangers have prayed, donated, and offered to be tested.

And yet, the one compatible donor I desperately need has not been found.

Elon, you build rockets that reach beyond this planet. You lead companies developing artificial intelligence capable of solving problems once thought impossible. You own a platform that connects people across the world in seconds.

Could we use some of that extraordinary technology to help find one compatible human being?

I’m not asking for SpaceX stock. I’m not asking for a check. I’m asking you to help demonstrate that the future of technology can be measured not only in dollars, discoveries, and destinations, but in lives changed.

And imagine if this effort helped not just me, but thousands of transplant patients whose compatible donors are somewhere in the world, waiting to be found.

You’ve challenged humanity to think bigger.

I’m asking you to help us think bigger about saving lives.

Separation vs Integration

The debate between separation and integration has long defined the struggle for self-determination among Foundational Black / Antebellum-Black / Anglo-Black / Anglo-Moor Americans. Traditionally, integration is viewed as the path to equality through inclusion, while separation is seen as a means to build independent autonomy. However, an analysis of the modern political landscape reveals a stark reality: as long as Foundational Black / Antebellum-Black / Anglo-Black Americans remain a minority in all 50 states, neither strategy can truly work in their favor. Without a critical mass of population and structural governing authority, integration often results in cultural and economic absorption, while separation leads to isolated, under-resourced enclaves.
The fundamental flaw in both models under the current demographic distribution is the absence of systemic power. For integration or separation to yield true equity, Foundational-Black / Antebellum-Black / Anglo-Black Americans would require a super majority population and governing control over a distinct geographic region, specifically in the core Southern states like North Carolina, South Carolina, Georgia, Alabama, Mississippi, Louisiana, Arkansas, and Tennessee. Flipping the demographic dynamic changes the entire power calculus. In a scenario where Anglo-Black / Anglo-Moor Americans hold a super majority in these states, the terms of engagement shift entirely. Integration would no longer mean Foundation Black / Anglo-Black Americans assimilating into dominant white institutions; instead, the white population would have to integrate into a society governed and structured by the Anglo-Black super majority. Conversely, separation becomes viable because the community would be large, self-sustaining, and economically independent enough to function successfully with or without the broader white population.
Furthermore, neither social integration nor physical separation can succeed without institutional teeth. True autonomy requires governing power. Because the 50 states within the American Federalist system hold nearly all the attributes, legal rights, and functions of an independent country, any successful movement requires state-level machinery. An ethnic minority scattered thinly across municipal lines cannot fully leverage the law. Foundational Black / Antebellum-Moor / Anglo-Moor Americans would need an entity like a state government to effectively exercise U.S. Constitutional Powers, dictate local commerce, command law enforcement, and control educational curricula.
To bridge the gap between this political theory and reality, strategic frameworks like the one proposed by Frederick Delk offer a blueprint for consolidation. Delk argues that Foundational Black / Anglo-Black / Anglo-Moor Americans should establish their own independent Political Party and intentionally consolidate 80% of their national population within the designated 8 State Southern Region. By migrating to and concentrating voting power within NC, SC, GA, AL, MS, LA, AR, and TN, Antebellum-Black / Anglo-Black / Anglo-Moor Americans could convert latent demographic numbers into a solid political bloc.
The traditional concepts of separation and integration are ineffective for a permanent minority. Real progress requires a shift from seeking acceptance or isolation toward geographical consolidation and institutional capture. By concentrating population in the South and organizing an independent Political Party, Antebellum-Black / Antebellum-Moor Americans (Historical), Foundational-Black/ Anglo-Black / Anglo-Moor Americans (Modern) could acquire the state-level governing control necessary to make self-determination a reality.

Stanford's free course catalog extends far beyond AI and computer science. Over 2,100 courses are available across virtually every academic discipline  many of them auditable for free through Coursera, edX, or Stanford's own online platform.

What's available:

Computer Science: algorithms, data structures, cryptography, networking, databases, cybersecurity, human-computer interaction.

Business: strategy, innovation, organizational behavior, finance, marketing, entrepreneurship, negotiations.

Medicine and Health: nutrition science, epidemiology, health policy, wellness, biomedical informatics, global health.

Humanities: philosophy, history, literature, writing, ethics, psychology.

Engineering: electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, energy systems, nanotechnology.

Mathematics and Data Science: statistics, probability, linear algebra, data mining, data analysis.

How to access them:

https://t.co/o4Z7hSKuGO: search "Stanford University." Most courses offer free auditing  you access all video lectures, readings, and some assignments without paying. A certificate (optional) costs $49-$79.

https://t.co/IIR18s79DM: search "Stanford." Similar free auditing model.

https://t.co/CKUTq5UjWf: Stanford's own portal with free webinars, lectures, and select courses.

The important distinction: "free" means free access to the educational content  lectures, readings, discussions. Certificates, grades, and credentials usually require payment. The knowledge is free. The proof is not.

News Flashback

Jan-March 2026

Streaming Wars

The "Streaming Wars" refers to the intense competition among digital media platforms to dominate the subscription video-on-demand (SVOD) market by capturing and retaining global audiences.

As of early 2026, the landscape has shifted from a period of rapid expansion into a phase of major consolidation and a focus on profitability over subscriber volume.

The "Winner" (2026)

Netflix Dominance: Industry analysts increasingly cite Netflix as the victor. In January 2026, Netflix reported 18% year-over-year revenue growth and is currently pursuing a high-stakes $83 billion all-cash acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery’s studio and streaming assets (including HBO/Max).

The "Big 3": Despite fierce competition, the market is primarily dominated by Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, and Disney+.

YouTube's Rise: Some experts argue YouTube is the true winner of the broader attention economy, surpassing traditional streaming services in total viewership by pivoting back to user-generated content.

Key Strategies in 2026

Consolidation: Smaller or struggling services are being shuttered or merged. For example, Disney recently shut down Hulu as a standalone service.

Monetization Shifts: Platforms have moved away from "growth at all costs" to strategies like password-sharing crackdowns, ad-supported tiers, and price hikes.

Live Sports & Events: Services are increasingly bidding on live sports rights (e.g., Netflix hosting WWE's Raw starting in 2025) to differentiate their offerings.

Bundling: To combat "subscription fatigue," platforms are forming strategic partnerships with telecommunications companies and banks to offer bundled service hubs.

Consumer Impact

Price Hikes: Many consumers are canceling services due to rising costs; over 40% of Americans cited price as their primary reason for unsubscribing in late 2025.

Resurgence of Piracy: Fragmented content and high costs have led to a significant comeback for pirate sites, which some users now find more comprehensive than paid services.

"South Park: The Streaming Wars": The term was popularized in mainstream culture by a 2-part South Park special released on Paramount+ in 2022, which satirized the industry's aggressive competition.

Gold (1974)

Gold is a 1974 British action-thriller directed by Peter R. Hunt, starring Roger Moore and Susannah York. Based on the 1970 novel Gold Mine by Wilbur Smith, the film is set in the South African goldfields and follows a conspiracy by a global syndicate to manipulate the price of gold by sabotaging a rich mine.

Plot: Rod Slater (Moore), a newly appointed general manager, is manipulated by his boss, Manfred Steyner (Bradford Dillman), into drilling through a protective barrier into a subterranean lake. This is intended to flood the mine, causing a global gold shortage and driving up prices for a greedy cabal.

Production Controversy: The film was controversially shot on location in South Africa during the apartheid era. This led to a "black ban" by British film unions, though some crew members defied it to work on the production.

James Bond Connection: Many crew members were veterans of the James Bond franchise, including director Peter Hunt (On Her Majesty's Secret Service), editor John Glen, and title designer Maurice Binder.

Accolades: The film received an Academy Award nomination for Best Original Song for "Wherever Love Takes Me," composed by Elmer Bernstein and sung by Maureen McGovern.

New Delaware businesses can now run their state permits and inspections through one coordinated process.

Gov. Matt Meyer launched the Small Business Joint Inspection Pilot on Monday, October 19. It comes from Section 5 of Executive Order 21, which he signed in May and which created the Office of Small Business Access. That office, led by Director Anastasia Jackson, runs the pilot.

The state says a new owner used to have to apply to several agencies and search different websites to learn what each one required. Now owners entering through Delaware One Stop are offered the program, and it's voluntary. The state tells them which permits, licenses, and applications their business needs, and the Office of Small Business Access helps line up the inspection visits. Agencies get an alert as soon as a new business enters the process, so they can plan their reviews. Owners may also get local planning, zoning, and business license contacts for their address.

It's only for owners who haven't opened yet and need to complete applications with participating state agencies. You have to create a https://t.co/7uK5IxKhTy account.

Alberta has rapidly transformed into a world-class powerhouse for Hollywood and international filmmakers. Major blockbusters like The Last of Us, Interstellar.
Metallica: Enter Sandman
https://t.co/3kNN2cWXtm
The Revenant, and Ghostbusters: 
Afterlife have chosen the province not just for a single scene, but as the primary backdrop for their massive productions. 

The visual versatility, world-class local expertise, and highly strategic economic environment drive Alberta's mass appeal to Hollywood.

1. Geographic Versatility and Unique Visuals
Alberta’s landscapes can replicate almost any location in the world. 

The "Chameleon" Terrain: 
Within a few hours of driving, a production crew can access the jagged peaks of the Rocky Mountains, rolling agricultural prairies, harsh desert badlands, and modern urban skylines. 

Alberta has effortlessly doubled for the post-apocalyptic United States (The Last of Us), midwestern Kansas (Interstellar), Wyoming (Brokeback Mountain), and the freezing wilderness of 1820s America (The Revenant).

The Quality of Light: 
Filmmakers frequently praise Alberta's specific northern light and long golden hours. 

Southern Alberta also benefits from Chinook winds, giving it a longer, less snow-heavy shooting window than other northern regions, which saves studios massive logistical costs.

2. Aggressive Financial Incentives and Tax Structures
While geography gets Hollywood's attention, the math seals the deal.

Uncapped Film & Television Tax Credit (FTTC): 
Alberta offers a highly competitive, refundable tax credit. 

Productions can claim a base of 22%, which scales up to 30% for Alberta-led productions or projects utilizing rural and remote filming streams (such as shooting in smaller towns like Fort Macleod or Lethbridge). 

Crucially, the provincial government removed the previous $10-million cap per project, allowing massive, high-budget studio projects to claim credits on their entire eligible local spend.

No Provincial Sales Tax (PST): 
Unlike other major filming hubs in Canada (like British Columbia or Ontario), Alberta has 0% provincial sales tax. 

When a studio is spending tens of millions of dollars on equipment rentals, catering, accommodations, and construction, saving 7% to 8% upfront provides an enormous financial discount.

The Exchange Rate: 
The built-in advantage of a weaker Canadian dollar gives American studios an automatic discount on their purchasing power. 

3. Elite Crew Infrastructure and Industry Recognition
Hollywood no longer needs to fly in an entire workforce; Alberta has built its own elite infrastructure. 

Weather-Tested Crews: 
Alberta is home to highly skilled, unionized technicians, set designers, and camera crews. 

Crucially, local crews are world-renowned for their ability to manage complex, extreme climate conditions—whether filming in freezing mountain blizzards or blistering prairie winds—without letting production stall.

“Key fraud-related reporting (2024)
The main contemporaneous press coverage is from the Minnesota Reformer (June 5, 2024, by Max Nesterak), widely cited and republished elsewhere:
•  In fall 2021, D.C.-area restaurant owner Naeem Mohd was offered a chance to invest $300,000 in the new California winery (eStCru) with the promise of tripling his money (200% return) in 18 months, plus 10% monthly interest if late. The pitch came via Tim Mynett (Omar’s husband since 2020) and longtime partner Will Hailer (they had co-founded political consultancy E Street Group). ￼
•  Mohd wired the money. The promised return never materialized on time. Mynett and Hailer later returned the $300,000 principal (about a month late). A California lawsuit (filed ~fall 2023) sought at least $780,000 and alleged they “fraudulently misrepresented … that estCru, LLC was a legitimate company.” ￼
•  Mynett and Hailer (via attorneys) denied deliberate fraud or conspiracy, saying the business struggled in a tough industry (including COVID effects) and that suggestions of intentional wrongdoing were false and defamatory. The winery did produce some wines (with winemaker Erica Stancliff) under names such as Blockchain, Overt, and The Devil’s Lie. Related reporting noted separate financial issues involving Hailer and cannabis ventures. ￼
The civil case later settled (around November 2024). No criminal charges tied to the winery allegations have been reported. ￼
Winery shutdown reporting (2026)
Multiple outlets reported that eStCru was formally terminated/ceased operations on April 4, 2026, per California business records (signed by Hailer):
•  New York Post (April 24, 2026): “Ilhan Omar husband’s California winery closes its doors amid scrutiny of congresswoman’s family finances.” It noted the timing relative to a February 2026 House Oversight letter from Chairman James Comer questioning large valuation jumps. ￼
•  Fox News (April 25, 2026): “Winery belonging to Ilhan Omar’s husband shut down amid financial spotlight.” eStCru shut down as of April 4 while Comer’s committee probed assets that surged in Omar’s disclosures. ￼
•  Washington Free Beacon, Washington Times, Daily Wire, and others published similar accounts of the April 4 termination. A spokesperson had previously described the winery as no longer operational. ￼
The closure occurred amid congressional scrutiny of Omar’s financial disclosures. Those forms showed the couple’s related assets (eStCru stake and Rose Lake Capital, another Mynett/Hailer venture) jumping from low tens of thousands in 2023 to ranges totaling up to ~$30 million in 2024. Omar later amended the 2024 filing downward (to under $100k total assets in the revised version), attributing the earlier figures to accounting errors that listed assets without full liabilities. Comer’s February 2026 letter specifically referenced the earlier investor lawsuit and questions about how the winery’s reported value rose so sharply. Court records had shown the company with very low cash balances (e.g., ~$650 at one point while defending the suit). ￼
Summary of what the reports actually show: Civil fraud allegations (misrepresentation about the legitimacy of the investment) in a settled lawsuit, followed by the winery’s formal termination in April 2026 during a congressional probe into the large reported valuation swings on Omar’s disclosures. It was not a government-ordered shutdown for proven criminal fraud; the civil case settled without criminal charges. Primary sources for the fraud claims are the 2024 Minnesota Reformer piece and the underlying California complaint; the shutdown coverage is concentrated in April 2026 outlets citing California Secretary of State records.”
